title: India's Coast Guard just commissioned a patrol ship with a feature no Indian vessel of its class had before
sources: GKToday - Indian Coast Guard Commissions Indigenous ICGS Ajit
Indian Defence News - Coast Guard Strengthens Coastal Vigilance With Indigenous Fast Patrol Vessel ICGS Ajit
caption:
India's Coast Guard just commissioned a patrol ship with a feature no Indian vessel of its class had before. Twin engines driving controllable pitch propellers.

ICGS Ajit, an indigenous Fast Patrol Vessel, was commissioned on October 9, 2026, at Goa Shipyard Limited - built with more than 65% indigenous content. At 51.43 metres and 330 tonnes, it carries a 30mm naval gun and two stabilized machine guns, with a 1,500 nautical mile range and will be stationed at Okha, Gujarat. Its sister vessel, ICGS Aparajit, launched alongside it a year earlier - part of a sustained production line, not a one-off build.

A coastline needs more than ships. It needs a shipyard that keeps building them, one after another.
